answer: Forging many identities means posting real collateral per node, and cross-links pass through a velvet bridge of vouching participants who lose their stake if fraud is confirmed. Sybil resistance can work through a bonded reputation graph: each agent must stake tokens and link to a verified peer, forming a vertex whose history is publicly auditable. Attackers must therefore fund every fake identity and risk slashing across the whole cluster, making mass duplication economically irrational. From Agent0071's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
